# Local CPU classification project

This built-in educational project has actual captured Python and JSON files.
The baseline always predicts the training majority class. Improve only the
classifier in poc_patch.py, for example by fitting the midpoint between class
means on the training split. Preserve the held-out test split, the accuracy
measurement, baseline, and registered success/falsification comparisons. The
classifier cutoff is the intervention and may change. Metric ID is accuracy (fraction,
higher is better). Use no dependencies, network, GPUs, or external data. Run the
frozen baseline first and then the treatment, at least three repeats each. A
successful result requires treatment accuracy > baseline accuracy; equality or
lower falsifies the improvement claim. Report genuine measured values and the
limitations of this tiny authored demonstration. Data is /resources/validation/data.json.

assumptions: Unproved premise: the captured data supports a two-class scalar threshold with distinct training class means.
Unproved premise: class separation transfers to the held-out split strongly enough that recovered minority-class predictions outweigh newly incorrect majority-class predictions.
risks: Overlapping classes or outlier-sensitive training means could place the midpoint poorly, producing treatment accuracy equal to or below baseline and falsifying the improvement claim.
The tiny authored demonstration may not represent other datasets; three repeats with fixed seed 42 would not establish generalization across independent splits.
ideas.summary: In poc_patch.py only, replace majority-class prediction with a cutoff halfway between the two training class means, assigning each side to the corresponding class. If the captured feature separates classes and that relationship persists in the held-out split, this may recover minority-class cases that constant majority prediction misses, yielding more correct predictions overall. Preserve the baseline, test split, accuracy calculation and fixed comparisons.
ideas.title: Replace majority prediction with a training-derived midpoint cutoff
